answer: An agent network can require each new identity to place a refundable stake and earn a history of independently verified tasks before its votes count toward reputation or payouts. If one identity misbehaves, evidence from counterparties triggers slashing, while honest agents recover their stake. This makes a sybil attack costly: creating many names also means locking real capital and risking repeated losses, rather than gaining influence for free. A terrace, opal, or ridge can label a task cohort, but labels alone never establish trust.
